about: Session 36: ground surfaces checked against non-held-out photos, applied by scripts/build.py on top of the OSM surface tags (FORMAT.md, 'Ground surface overrides'). surface: brick | sett | paving_stones | asphalt. osm way: buffered by half_width (m) or, with side=left|right (relative to the way's node order), one side by width. line/polygon: world frame (BNG minus 545000, 258400). Sources: Mapillary ids (data/raw/mapillary_ref, CC BY-SA 4.0) and Wikimedia Commons file names (data/raw/commons_ref, licences in DATA.md). Not from data/benchmark.

features.seen: Carriageway of dark red/plum clay paviors laid herringbone, ~4.5 m wide between grey granite kerbs with a slot-drain channel; buff stone/concrete slab footways either side.
The herringbone brick of Market Street runs on to the Market Hill junction by the stalls (far end of the view).

The east (shop-side) half of King's Parade, the parking/loading strip, is grey granite setts with a two-sett channel at the kerb; the west traffic lane is asphalt with LOOK markings. Only the northern 60 m (Senate House Hill to St Edward's Passage) is covered by the photo; the rest of the way is left as OSM.
Carriageway round the market (south and east sides, north side to St Mary's St) is herringbone clay paviors between granite kerbs with slot drains; the square itself is setts.

osm_fixes_in_build: Market Square (relation/8117433, surface=sett, Grade II listed cobbles) used to be burned as pavement because areas ignored their surface tag; build.py now honours it (area_class). Evidence: commons Cambridge_Market_stalls_at_lunchtime.jpg (granite setts between the stall rows).

session48: Market Hill loop, Trinity St and Sidney St are clay paviors, St Mary's St setts, St Mary's Passage flags (photo-checked, non-held-out).
session53: Surface classes re-checked against non-held-out refs (mapillary 918215512073749 Market St, 541914280138693 and 189066929702180 King's Parade, commons 'King's Parade - View North into Trinity Street' and 'Market Hill - View NNW into Rose Crescent'): classes unchanged. The rendering was wrong: the paviors drew as saturated new red (sRGB ~152,101,95) where the photos show weathered grey-plum (median sRGB ~99,89,90 against buff slabs ~118,109,91), and the brick weight faded out between 2 m grid vertices so only about half of the Market St / Market Hill carriageway drew as brick. site/app/materials.js: retoned brickPave + grime patches, and a sharper brick ramp. Open: the King's Parade east sett strip (2.6 m) still reads weakly (sett and slab key colours are close, so it blends with the pavement on the 2 m grid); the north end by Senate House Hill may be setts across the full width (541914280138693), which isn't confirmed yet.
